---
title: "Installing METIS"
---

METIS is a Python package. We use [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to install it
and manage its dependencies.

## Installation with uv

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and
[Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads), then:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git
cd metis
uv sync
```

That's it. uv installs Python, METIS and the dependencies for the walkthrough,
including plotting and JupyterLab. The checkout already selects a CPU-compatible
PyTorch build, so there is no PyTorch configuration to edit.

Check the installation with:

```bash
uv run metis demo --steps 100
```

This short installation check saves a model and predictions in `metis-demo/`.
It uses an explicitly reduced SIRDS subset; the walkthrough uses the full bank.
Run Python scripts with `uv run python your_script.py`.

## Using METIS in your own project

You can also install METIS as a dependency without cloning its repository.
Inside an existing uv project, run:

```bash
uv add "metis-surrogate[docs] @ git+https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git"
```

For a new project, first run `uv init my-surrogate --python 3.13` and
`cd my-surrogate`. Then use the command above. Future installations of your
project only need `uv sync`; keep `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` with your work.

`[docs]` includes the notebook and plotting tools used here. Omit it if you only
need the library. The distribution is **metis-surrogate**, imported as **metis**;
it is not yet on PyPI. The PyPI package named `metis` is unrelated.

## Running the notebooks

Each worked example shows its executed outputs. Under **Other Formats**, choose
**Jupyter** to download it, then open it with:

```bash
uv run jupyter lab
```

Alternatively, choose **Open in Colab**, then **Runtime → Run all**. Its first
cell gets the matching METIS revision and runs `uv sync` in the notebook
interpreter, keeping Colab's unrelated packages. A new runtime needs setup
again. Colab sometimes preloads libraries: if it reports a version conflict or
requests a restart, restart once and run all cells again.

::: {.callout-note}
The tutorials run on CPU. For NVIDIA GPUs or a smaller CPU-only installation
in your own project, see the [optional PyTorch setup](https://github.com/OJWatson/metis/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#optional-pytorch-setup).
Python 3.11+ and Linux, Windows or Apple Silicon macOS are supported; the current
PyTorch dependency range does not support Intel Macs.
:::
